extracted.intended_audience: telecommunications licensees, applicants, siting authorities, and broadband/data reporting entities interacting with FCC Part 1 rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory compliance rules from FCC Part 1 covering foreign ownership rulings and notifications, reasonable periods for state/local action on wireless siting applications (shot clocks and tolling), eligible facilities modification standards, and FCC Form 477 reporting and confidentiality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insertion of wholly-owned foreign subsidiary does not require prior approval (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: The insertion of a wholly-owned, foreign-organized subsidiary into the vertical ownership chain between a foreign-organized entity and a U.S. parent or U.S. corporation, where there are no other changes in the direct or indirect foreign ownership of the U.S. entity, would not require prior Commission approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two illustrative examples are provided showing: (a) a Foreign Subsidiary inserted between Foreign Company and U.S. Parent A, and (b) a Foreign Subsidiary inserted between Foreign Company and U.S. Corporation A, in each case with no other ownership changes; such insertions do not require prior Commission approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when an unapproved foreign-organized entity is inserted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a previously unapproved foreign-organized entity is inserted into the vertical ownership chain of a licensee or its controlling U.S.-organized parent without prior Commission approval pursuant to paragraph (d)(1), the licensee shall file a letter to the attention of the Chief, Office of International Affairs (or Chief, Media Bureau for broadcast licensees), within 30 days after the insertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter must include the name of the new foreign-organized entity and a certification by the licensee that the entity complies with the 100 percent common ownership and control requirement in paragraph (d)(1). The letter must reference the licensee's foreign ownership ruling(s) by ICFS File No. and FCC Record citation if available; for broadcast licensees, reference CDBS File No., Docket No., call sign(s), facility ID(s), and FCC Record citation, if available. Notification is not required if the ownership change is the subject of a pro forma application or pro forma notification already filed pursuant to the relevant service rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: New petition required before exceeding authorized foreign ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee that has received a foreign ownership ruling (including a U.S.-organized successor-in-interest formed as part of a pro forma reorganization), or any subsidiary or affiliate relying on such ruling, shall file a new petition for declaratory ruling under § 1.5000 to obtain Commission approval before its foreign ownership exceeds the routine terms and conditions of this section and/or any specific terms or conditions of its ruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing compliance: duty to notify Commission of non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified in paragraph (f)(3), if at any time the licensee (including successors-in-interest and subsidiaries/affiliates relying on the ruling) knows or has reason to know that it is no longer in compliance with its foreign ownership ruling or the Commission's foreign ownership rules, it shall file a statement with the Commission explaining the circumstances within 30 days of the date it knew or had reason to know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent remedial actions do not relieve the obligation to notify the Commission of the circumstances (including duration) of non-compliance. Such licensee and any controlling companies, whether U.S.- or foreign-organized, may be subject to enforcement action including orders requiring divestiture of direct and/or indirect interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on use of trusts/proxies to evade section 310(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual or entity that directly or indirectly creates or uses a trust, proxy, power of attorney, or any other contract, arrangement, or device with the purpose or effect of divesting itself, or preventing the vesting, of an equity or voting interest in the licensee (or in a controlling U.S. parent), as part of a plan or scheme to evade application of the Commission's rules or policies under section 310(b), shall be subject to enforcement action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement may include an order requiring divestiture of the investor's direct and/or indirect interests in such entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial petition process and conditions for eligible U.S. public companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the controlling U.S. parent of certain licensees is an eligible U.S. public company (§ 1.5000(e)), the licensee may file a remedial petition for declaratory ruling under § 1.5000(a)(1) (or (a)(2) for publicly traded common carriers) seeking approval of particular foreign equity/voting interests that are non-compliant; alternatively the licensee may remedy non-compliance (e.g., redeem foreign interests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements/exceptions include: (i) licensee must notify the relevant Bureau by letter no later than 10 days after learning of the investments that rendered it non-compliant and specify that it will file a petition or remedy within 30 days; (ii) the licensee shall demonstrate in its petition (or letter showing timely remedy) that the non-compliance was due solely to circumstances beyond its control not reasonably foreseeable with due diligence; (iii) during pendency of a petition under § 1.5000(a)(1) the Commission will not require redemption of the non-compliant interest, but if petition is denied the licensee must have a mechanism to come into compliance within 30 days of the Commission's decision; (iv) Commission reserves the right to require immediate remedial action where public interest—e.g., national security—requires such action. Note: paragraph (f)(3) provisions referring to petitions under (a)(1) are to be read as referring to (a)(2) for paragraph (f)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart U purpose (wireless siting rules implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart implements 47 U.S.C. 332(c)(7) and 1455.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to siting and small wireless facilities (action, antenna, antenna equipment, antenna facility, applicant, authorization, collocation, deployment, facility, siting application, siting authority, structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms used in this subpart are defined (e.g., 'Action' means a siting authority's grant or written denial; 'Antenna' consistent with § 1.1320(d) means apparatus designed to emit RF radiation for personal wireless service; 'Collocation' means mounting/installing an antenna facility on a pre-existing structure or modifying a structure for that purpose; 'Siting authority' means state/local government or instrumentality whose authorization is necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions point to cross-referenced provisions (e.g., § 1.1320(d)) and clarify inclusion/exclusion (e.g., antenna does not include unintentional radiator, mobile station, or part 15 device).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and eligibility criteria for 'Small wireless facilities'
rubrics_metrics.description: Small wireless facilities are facilities that meet each of the following conditions: (1) mounted on structures 50 feet or less in height including antennas, or mounted on structures no more than 10% taller than adjacent structures, or do not extend existing structures to >50 feet or by >10%; (2) each antenna (excluding associated antenna equipment) is no more than 3 cubic feet in volume; (3) all other wireless equipment associated with the structure is no more than 28 cubic feet in volume; (4) facilities do not require antenna structure registration under part 17; (5) facilities are not located on Tribal lands as defined under 36 CFR 800.16(x); and (6) facilities do not result in human exposure to RF radiation in excess of applicable safety standards specified in § 1.1307(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely action presumption (shot clock) for siting applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A siting authority that fails to act on a siting application on or before the shot clock date for the application is presumed not to have acted within a reasonable period of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shot clock period calculation (presumptively reasonable period + tolling)
rubrics_metrics.description: The shot clock period for a siting application is the sum of: (1) the number of days of the presumptively reasonable period for the type of application (per paragraph (c)), plus (2) the number of days of the tolling period, if any (per paragraph (d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively reasonable review periods by application type
rubrics_metrics.description: Presumptively reasonable periods for action on applications are: (i) collocate a Small Wireless Facility using an existing structure: 60 days; (ii) collocate a facility other than a Small Wireless Facility using an existing structure: 90 days; (iii) deploy a Small Wireless Facility using a new structure: 90 days; (iv) deploy a facility other than a Small Wireless Facility using a new structure: 150 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Batching rules: if a single application seeks authorization for multiple deployments all within category (i) or (iii), the period equals that for a single deployment in that category; if application mixes deployments that fall within (i) and (iii), the period for the whole application is 90 days. Siting authorities may not refuse to accept applications under these batching rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolling for materially incomplete applications and resubmissions (shot clock tolling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a written agreement provides otherwise, the tolling period is: (1) for initial Small Wireless Facilities: if siting authority notifies applicant on or before 10th day after submission that the application is materially incomplete and clearly/specifically identifies missing documents/information and the specific rule creating the obligation, the shot clock restarts at zero on the date applicant submits all identified items; (2) for other initial applications: tolling runs from day after siting authority's written notice of material incompleteness (if effectuated on or before 30th day after submission) until the date applicant submits all identified items; (3) for resubmissions following a notice of deficiency: tolling runs from day after notice that supplemental submission was insufficient (if effectuated on or before 10th day after supplemental submission) until applicant submits all identified items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices of incompleteness must clearly and specifically identify missing documents/info and the rule/regulation requiring them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shot clock date calculation and business day/holiday rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The shot clock date is determined by counting forward from the day after submission by the number of calendar days in the shot clock period (including any pre-application period asserted by the siting authority); if the calculated date is a 'holiday' per § 1.4(e)(1) or a legal holiday in the relevant State/local jurisdiction, the shot clock date is the next business day. 'Business day' is defined in § 1.4(e)(2) and excludes State/local legal holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for wireless facility modifications (base station, collocation, eligible facilities request, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms used in § 1.6100 are defined: 'Base station' means a structure or equipment at a fixed location enabling wireless communications between user equipment and a network (does not encompass a tower as defined in the subpart); 'Collocation' means mounting/installation of transmission equipment on an eligible support structure for transmitting/receiving RF signals; 'Eligible facilities request' means any request for modification of an existing tower or base station that does not substantially change the physical dimensions and involves collocation, removal, or replacement of transmission equipment; 'Eligible support structure' means any existing tower or base station at time of filing; 'Site' defined; 'Substantial change' criteria listed; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references provided for measurement and inclusion rules (e.g., how to measure increase in height).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial change criteria for eligible support structures
rubrics_metrics.description: A modification substantially changes the physical dimensions of an eligible support structure if it meets any of these criteria: (i) increases height of tower (non-ROW) by >10% or by height of one additional antenna array with separation ≤20 feet, whichever greater; for other structures, increases height by >10% or >10 feet, whichever greater (measurement rules specified); (ii) for towers other than ROW towers, adds an appurtenance protruding >20 feet (or more than width of tower at appurtenance level); for other structures, protrusion >6 feet; (iii) installation of more than the standard number of new equipment cabinets for the technology involved, but not to exceed four cabinets; or for ROW towers and base stations, installation of any new ground equipment cabinets if none pre-exist, or ground cabinets >10% larger in height or volume than other ground cabinets; (iv) entails excavation/deployment outside current site beyond specified limits (for towers other than ROW, >30 feet outside current site); (v) would defeat concealment elements; or (vi) does not comply with conditions associated with siting approval (with specified limitation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes measurement guidance for separated rooftop deployments and exclusions for previously approved appurtenances/modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval standard for eligible facilities requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A State or local government may not deny and shall approve any eligible facilities request for modification of an eligible support structure that does not substantially change the physical dimensions of such structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation limits for review of eligible facilities requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant asserts in writing that a request is covered by § 1.6100, a State or local government may require documentation or information only to the extent reasonably related to determining whether the request meets the requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A State or local government may not require any other documentation, including documentation intended to illustrate the need for the facilities or justify the business decision to modify the facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: 60-day timeframe for review of eligible facilities requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 60 days of the date on which an applicant submits a request seeking approval under § 1.6100, the State or local government shall approve the application unless it determines that the application is not covered by this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolling procedures for incompleteness under § 1.6100
rubrics_metrics.description: The 60-day period may be tolled only by mutual agreement or where reviewing authority determines the application is incomplete. To toll for incompleteness, the authority must provide written notice within 30 days of receipt clearly and specifically delineating all missing documents or information (limited to standards under paragraph (c)(1)). The timeframe begins running again when applicant makes supplemental submission; reviewing authority has 10 days to notify that supplemental submission remains insufficient. Second/subsequent notices may not specify missing items not delineated in the original notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to act deemed grant and applicant notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reviewing State or local government fails to approve or deny a request under § 1.6100 within the timeframe for review (accounting for tolling), the request shall be deemed granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deemed grant does not become effective until the applicant notifies the reviewing authority in writing after the review period has expired (accounting for any tolling) that the application has been deemed granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and judicial review for Section 6409(a) / § 1.6100 disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and reviewing authorities may bring claims related to Section 6409(a) to any court of competent jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart V purposes (collection of advanced telecommunications & competition data)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart sets out terms by which certain commercial and government-controlled entities report data to the Commission concerning provision of wired/wireless local telephone services and interconnected VoIP; deployment of advanced telecommunications capability; and availability/quality of broadband internet access service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for reporting (broadband connection, facilities-based provider, end user, local telephone service, mobile telephony service, broadband internet access service, broadband map, cell edge probability, cell loading, clutter, fabric, FCC Form 477, Indian Tribe, Mobility Fund Phase II, propagation model, provider, quality of service, shapefile, standard broadband installation, H3 indexing system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms used in the reporting subpart are defined (e.g., 'Broadband connection' means a line/channel/satellite service that terminates at an end user location or mobile device and enables info transfer rates exceeding 200 kbps in at least one direction; 'Facilities-based provider' defined by types of facilities; 'FCC Form 477' defined as the form relating to local telephone competition and broadband reporting; H3 geospatial indexing system described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions include technical thresholds (e.g., 200 kbps) and data format expectations (e.g., shapefile, H3), informing report content and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entities required to file FCC Form 477
rubrics_metrics.description: The following entities shall file a completed FCC Form 477 in accordance with rules and instructions: (1) Facilities-based providers of broadband service; (2) Providers of local telephone service; (3) Facilities-based providers of mobile telephony service; and (4) Providers of interconnected VoIP service to end users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification requirement for FCC Form 477 filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents identified shall include in each report a certification signed by an appropriate official of the respondent (as specified in the instructions to FCC Form 477) and shall report the title of their certifying official.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and confidentiality rules for Form 477 data
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency operations contact information in Form 477 should not be routinely available for public inspection pursuant to § 0.457, in addition to other nondisclosable information. Respondents may request that provider-specific subscription information be treated as confidential and withheld from public inspection by indicating so on Form 477 at submission. The Commission will release (and respondents may not request confidential treatment of): (A) provider-specific mobile deployment data; (B) data regarding minimum advertised or expected speeds for mobile broadband services; and (C) location information necessary for accurate broadband mapping, including crowdsourcing or challenge processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to treat other data as confidential must be submitted with the Form 477 filing along with reasons for withholding per § 0.459. The Commission makes all nondisclosure decisions, but Chiefs of specified Bureaus/Offices may release provider-specific info to (i) a state commission with adequate protections; (ii) 'eligible entities' as defined in the Broadband Data Improvement Act, in aggregated form under confidentiality conditions prescribed by the Commission; and (iii) others to the extent access can be provided in a manner that addresses competitive sensitivity and precludes public disclosure.
